fixes_applied.issue: keyboard focus indicator removed (WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible -- found by the keyboard-only pass, not by axe's default ruleset, which has no automated check for this)
fixes_applied.detail: `textarea:focus, input[type="text"]:focus { outline: none; ... }` and `select:focus { outline: none; ... }` are more specific than the page's generic `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid ...}` rule, so every text field and <select> lost its focus ring entirely on Tab, leaving only a subtle border-color shift (--rule -> --rule-firm) as the sole cue.
fixes_applied.fix: Removed `outline: none` from the plain :focus rules (kept the border-color change) and added textarea:focus-visible / input[type="text"]:focus-visible / select:focus-visible rules restoring the 2px solid outline for keyboard focus specifically.

fixes_applied.issue: fixed popup width causes horizontal scroll at narrow viewports (360px / 200% zoom check)
fixes_applied.detail: body { width: 400px } with no max-width forces a horizontal scrollbar whenever the available viewport is narrower than 400 CSS px.
fixes_applied.fix: Added max-width: 100% and overflow-x: hidden on body, plus max-width: 100% on html. Verified 400px baseline is unchanged; 360px viewport and 360px + document.documentElement.style.zoom=2 both show zero horizontal scroll after.

fixes_applied.issue: broken theme variables (CSS-only defect, not an axe violation because the affected elements are empty text at initial load)
fixes_applied.detail: popup.js sets inline style.color to var(--redact) and var(--text-muted) for status text (save/error states across server URL, full-page-capture, profile, pipeline, and planner selectors), but popup.html never defined either custom property. An undefined var() makes the whole `color` declaration compute as unset, which for the inherited `color` property falls back to the ancestor's color -- so the intended red/neutral state color silently never applied (not a contrast failure by luck, but the color-coding was inert).
fixes_applied.fix: Added --redact: var(--blocked) and --text-muted: var(--faint) aliases to :root so the existing inline styles resolve to the theme's real error/neutral colors, both already >=6.9:1 against --dark/--surface.

i18n.harness_change: run-audit.js switched from opening popup.html as a file:// page to serving extension/ over a throwaway local HTTP server (127.0.0.1, random port). Reason: the language toggle loads a locale's messages.json via fetch(browser.runtime.getURL(...)), and Chromium hard-blocks fetch() from a file:// origin to another file:// URL ('Failed to fetch') -- confirmed empirically, including with a Playwright route() intercept in place, which never even saw a routable request. A local static server sidesteps the restriction and is the closer analogue to the real chrome-extension:// origin anyway. --lang en|hi selects which locale the run boots into by having the stubbed chrome.storage.local.get('uiLang') answer with that value, exactly the shape a real prior toggle click leaves behind.
i18n.sanity_probe: each run reads document.documentElement.lang and the rendered .brand-sub text back out of the page BEFORE running axe, so a run that silently stayed in the wrong language (e.g. a fetch failure falling back to English) would be visible in this file rather than only in axe's language-agnostic pass/fail count.

i18n.result: 0 axe violations across all 4 states, in both languages. Keyboard reachability/focus-visibility, WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing, and the 360px/200% zoom check all pass identically in en and hi -- the Hindi (Devanagari) static text does not introduce any new clipping, overflow, or contrast failure. The consentPanel/goalPrivacyPanel axe states still use the pre-existing hardcoded-English test fixture text for those two dynamic panels (this harness sets it directly via page.evaluate to exercise axe against non-empty panels, independent of language) -- their structural accessibility (roles, focus, contrast) is language-agnostic and unaffected by which locale is active; the static, data-i18n-driven chrome around them (labels, buttons, hints, aria-labels) is what actually renders in Hindi and is what the sanity probe above confirms.
not_checked: Real screen-reader pronunciation/announcement of Devanagari text -- out of scope for axe/keyboard-mechanics checks, same limitation noted above for English.

The consent/goal-privacy panels' OWN dynamic sentences (built by extension/lib/action-describe.js's describePendingAction()/describePolicyReason(), now translate-aware) rendered live in Hindi through a real CONSENT_REQUEST/GOAL_PRIVACY_REVIEW_REQUEST round trip -- this harness fixture sets that panel text directly instead (see 'result' above); their Hindi wording is covered by tests/unit/test_action_describe.mjs (English-default behavior, unchanged) and tests/unit/test_i18n.mjs (key/placeholder parity), not by this axe run.
